Citizens and various groups marched Saturday to the EDSA People Power Monument to press for accountability amid the rampant corruption under the administration of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. This follows protests and university walkouts that came in the wake of Senate and House probes into the flood control fiasco, which implicated officials from the Department of Public Works and Highways and several lawmakers.

The groups called for the creation of a genuine independent commission that would include civil society organizations to investigate anomalous flood control and other infrastructure projects. 

“Bigyan ng totoong ngipin ang independent commission. Gawin ang spirit of the law. Dapat makita ang lahat ng mga tinatago,” said Kiko Aquino Dee, co-convenor of the Tindig Pilipinas coalition.

They also pointed to the persistence of systemic corruption even after the 1986 EDSA Revolution, citing the creation of the Priority Development Assistance Fund in 2000, which later exploded into the 2012 pork barrel scam. Among those implicated was Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, whose name also surfaced in the current controversy.

Meanwhile, Kabataan Party-List Rep. Renee Co criticized the government’s substandard projects, claiming funds were funneled directly into the pockets of district engineers and other officials while leaving communities vulnerable to floods during calamities. 

“Ang hamon natin ngayon sa kabataan: Ang galit [ay] ‘wag nating hayaang mawala. Aalalahanin natin ang gutom na nararanasan at bahang nilulusong natin,” Co said.

The groups will reconvene for a larger protest at Luneta Park on Sept. 21, coinciding with the commemoration of the Martial Law declaration.

Photos by Lemuel Pabalan

ICYMI: All U.P. Workers Union–UP Manila/PGH (AUPWU-Manila/PGH), together with the UP Manila University Student Council, unfurled their banner at the PGH Quadrangle to manifest unity in denouncing corruption and demanding higher state subsidy for UP-PGH employees yesterday, Sept. 12. 

“Nakikiisa tayo sa panawagan ng mga iskolar ng bayan laban sa korapsyon. Hindi hiwalay ang UPM at PGH dahil ang mga proyekto ng unibersidad, ilan ay nasa ilalim ng DPWH,” said AUPWU-Manila/PGH president Karen Faurillo.

The union asserted that relentless budget cuts and corruption are the root causes of the flooding around PGH. They demand accountability and transparency to protect the welfare of students and healthcare workers.
